expected.note: Notice amount; summary judgment granted for respondent on all issues; sustained in full.
expected.snippet: Respondent determined a deficiency of $14,650 in petitioner's Federal income tax and an accuracy-related penalty of $2,875

expected.note: Total retirement distributions (Fidelity 401(k) $1,375 + Northern Trust employer plan $85,025) held includible; petitioner had reported $45,025, so $41,375 omitted.
expected.snippet: show that petitioner received $86,400 in taxable retirement income in 2016, rather than the $45,025 reported on his return

expected.note: Court relies on the $14,650 deficiency exceeding $5,000.
expected.snippet: respondent has satisfied his burden of production by clearly demonstrating a "substantial understatement of income tax."

expected.note: 6751(b) approval not required (automatically calculated through electronic means, AUR); no reasonable cause shown.
expected.snippet: Accordingly, we sustain respondent's determination to impose the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty.

expected.note: Notice amount stated by the court and sustained. Not mechanically 20% of $14,650 (would be $2,930), so the penalty base differs from the deficiency.
expected.snippet: Respondent determined that petitioner is liable for a $2,875 accuracyrelated penalty.

issues_outside_coverage: Summary judgment under Rule 121 (procedural; petitioner failed to respond)
Section 6751(b)(2)(B) exception for penalties automatically calculated through electronic means (decided as part of the 6662 issue)
decisive_judgment_findings: Petitioner failed to respond to the summary judgment motion and court order, leaving no genuine dispute of material fact.
Third-party declarations, Forms 1099-R and a check established receipt of $1,375 (Fidelity 401(k)) and $85,025 (Northern Trust employer plan).
No evidence offered of any 72(t) exception.
AUR program computed the penalty automatically, so no supervisory approval was required.
No reasonable cause argument or evidence.

unscored_items.note: Court sustains liability for the 10% additional tax but states no amount and does not say whether the base is the $41,375 omitted or the full $86,400; no value given.
unscored_items.snippet: we sustain respondent's determination that petitioner is liable for the 10% additional tax
